msg: The important part of the gnomes is the colour of their hat - their position and the size of their hat doesn't matter. If they are orange, red, blue, or green then you will go to a bright forest. If their hat is brown, pink, purple, or yellow then you will go to a dark forest. In each pair of gnomes, there will be one that takes you to the bright forest and one that takes you to the dark forest. The forests change how many mushrooms they have over time, so first decide if you want to be in a bright forest or a dark forest then keep an eye on how many mushrooms you are getting to figure out if you are making the right choice.Some tips:'Good' forests generally give at least 4 mushrooms. If you are aiming for the bright forest (for example) but keep getting 2 or less mushrooms, get to the dark forest instead. The highest amount of mushrooms I saw was 9. The lowest was 0.It's a lot easier to memorise the colours for one forest, then work backwards for the other. e.g. I memorised colours for the bright forest - I kept repeating to myself orange, red, blue, green will get me to the bright forest. That meant the other colours had to be the dark forest if that's where I wanted to be. To repeat:Bright forest: red, orange, blue, greenDark forest: yellow, brown, purple, pinkThe gnomes always show up in the same pairs. Red-yellow. Orange-brown. Blue-purple. Green-pink.You will get a few rounds in a row where one forest gives a high amount of mushrooms. When the number of mushroom falls a lot, swap to the other forest. You will have to keep swapping throughout the game.
